findings.title: Unknown future events bypass universal output and lifecycle relation completeness
findings.reproduction: At exact candidate f2c9c0aa6539af0067bf76711883b22a796ddbf3, load the valid source-acquisition fixture in either generated runtime, change type to org.research-observatory.future.observed.v2 and activityType to future-observation, leave the exact bound output and subject in place, and remove every relation except wasAssociatedWith. provenanceEventErrors/provenance_event_errors returns no errors even though the output has neither wasGeneratedBy nor wasAttributedTo. Then change activity.status to failed without removing the output; both runtimes still return no errors. The generic relation-role and outcome checks inspect only relations that happen to exist, while known-event shape and exact relation completeness are now entirely inside the knownActivity block. This regresses the R01 implementation's universal input/output completeness and permits T02 to persist an orphan output or a material output for an activity that explicitly failed. Unknown catalog meaning may remain uninterpreted, but the contract's own inputs, outputs, activity status, actor, and W3C PROV relation semantics are not unknown and must remain internally complete.
findings.required_remediation: Enforce type-independent structural provenance invariants before the known-event policy branch. Non-succeeded activities must not carry outputs. Every succeeded output must have exactly one wasGeneratedBy and wasAttributedTo relation to its exact revision and responsible agent; every input claimed as used must remain exact, and any derivation/invalidation fact must obey the existing role and outcome rules. Keep known types' stricter acquisition/transformation/invalidation matrices, but allow a future type only when its chosen structural shape is internally complete without assigning catalog meaning. Add matching TypeScript, Python, and schema-metadata tests for a valid unknown acquisition-like event, valid unknown transformation-like event, orphan succeeded output, failed output, missing attribution, and exact revision closure.

findings.title: Stable entity kind and the claimed UUID namespace remain inconsistent
findings.reproduction: The candidate's own transformEvent/transform_event fixture copies the source entity, keeps the same stable entityId, changes only revisionId, and then changes entityKind from source-observation to document. Both generated runtimes return no errors for every lifecycle status, and the test describes the succeeded form as a valid same-stable-entity revision transformation. ADR-0013 and docs/architecture/local-sqlite-storage.md make aggregate identity and kind immutable across revisions; accepting this event lets one stable identity change meaning and makes lineage by entityId ambiguous even though relation endpoints now carry exact revisions. Independently, set the fixture's UUIDv7 projectid equal to the event id and update the exact subject's project prefix; both runtimes return no errors because globalIds excludes projectid, despite the R02 evidence claiming a global UUID namespace collision check. The subject grammar is also narrower than the governed PortableKey entityKind grammar: source.observation is a valid entityKind but no exact entity subject containing that kind can pass. These are contract-level identity inconsistencies that T02 persistence cannot safely infer away.
findings.required_remediation: Require every occurrence of one stable entityId in an event to retain one entityKind; update the valid same-entity revision fixture to preserve kind. A cross-kind transformation must mint a distinct stable entity identity and link the exact output revision to the exact input revision. Include a UUIDv7 project identity in the relevant collision set, or document and test a narrowly justified namespace exception instead of claiming global uniqueness. Harmonize the exact-subject kind segment with the accepted entityKind grammar, either by using one safely encodable grammar in both places or by narrowing the portable kind contract consistently. Add TypeScript and Python tests for same-ID/same-kind revisions, same-ID/different-kind denial, distinct-ID/cross-kind derivation, project/event collision, and every accepted subject-kind spelling.

closures.evidence: The exact R01 known-event reproductions now fail in both generated runtimes. Denied, failed, and cancelled invalidation cannot assert wasInvalidatedBy; acquisition cannot add invalidation; used, generation, attribution, derivation, and invalidation endpoints are role-checked; and the known-event allowlist is status-aware. Fifteen TypeScript and seven Python cases cover all four statuses, wrong roles, and contradictory known relations. R02-F01 is a distinct forward-compatible completeness regression caused by moving universal output checks under knownActivity; it does not erase this concrete closure.

The prior unbound subject, subject-kind mismatch, duplicate relation ID/fact, and one-relation-for-two-revisions reproductions now fail. Relations carry composite entityId/revisionId endpoints, closure and completeness use those exact references, relation IDs/facts are unique, and a same-stable-ID/different-revision event can be represented. R02-F02 separately records the newly exposed immutable-kind, project-namespace, and subject-grammar inconsistencies rather than reopening the exact R01 ambiguity.

Schema, TypeScript, and Python all reject year zero and accept the explicit millisecond-Z UTC range from year 0001 through 9999.
